From 89d030804831c4075496629343ae3bb3ae8ff58f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Suraj Kandpal <suraj.kandpal@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2024 21:19:40 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] drm/xe/hdcp: Fix condition for hdcp gsc cs requirement

Add condition for check of hdcp gsc cs requirement rather than
assuming gsc cs to always be required when xe is loaded. It is not
required for display version < 14

--v2
-Use display version in commit message [Lucas]

Fixes: 152f2df954d8 ("drm/xe/hdcp: Enable HDCP for XE")
Signed-off-by: Suraj Kandpal <suraj.kandpal@intel.com>
Acked-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Uma Shankar <uma.shankar@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240308154939.1940960-2-suraj.kandpal@intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/display/xe_hdcp_gsc.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/display/xe_hdcp_gsc.c
index dcde1d0ac1f8..25c73602ef55 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/display/xe_hdcp_gsc.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/display/xe_hdcp_gsc.c
@@ -32,7 +32,7 @@ struct intel_hdcp_gsc_message {
 
 bool intel_hdcp_gsc_cs_required(struct xe_device *xe)
 {
-	return true;
+	return DISPLAY_VER(xe) >= 14;
 }
 
 bool intel_hdcp_gsc_check_status(struct xe_device *xe)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/display/xe_hdcp_gsc.c`**
   - The function `intel_hdcp_gsc_cs_required` was modified to change its return value. 
   - The original implementation returned `true` unconditionally, indicating that the HDCP GSC (Graphics Security Controller) is always required.
   - The modified implementation now returns a condition based on the display version: it returns `true` only if the display version is 14 or higher (`DISPLAY_VER(xe) >= 14`).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the `intel_hdcp_gsc_cs_required` function directly addresses a bug related to the assumption that HDCP GSC is always required when the XE (Xe Graphics) is loaded. 
- By introducing a conditional check based on the display version, the patch ensures that the requirement for HDCP GSC is accurately determined, thus preventing unnecessary enforcement of HDCP GSC for display versions lower than 14.
- This modification is part of a broader effort to enhance the functionality and correctness of the HDCP implementation in the XE graphics driver, as indicated by the fix reference to a previous commit.

Here is the commit message:
drm/xe/hdcp: Fix condition for hdcp gsc cs requirement

Add condition for check of hdcp gsc cs requirement rather than
assuming gsc cs to always be required when xe is loaded. It is not
required for display version < 14

--v2
-Use display version in commit message [Lucas]

Fixes: 152f2df954d8 ("drm/xe/hdcp: Enable HDCP for XE")
Signed-off-by: Suraj Kandpal <suraj.kandpal@intel.com>
Acked-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Uma Shankar <uma.shankar@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240308154939.1940960-2-suraj.kandpal@intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect assumption in the `intel_hdcp_gsc_cs_required` function that the HDCP GSC (Graphics Security Controller) is always required when the XE (Xe Graphics) is loaded, regardless of the display version. This led to situations where the requirement was enforced even for display versions lower than 14, where it is not necessary.

Here is the patch:
 
 bool intel_hdcp_gsc_cs_required(struct xe_device *xe)
 {
-	return true;
+	return DISPLAY_VER(xe) >= 14;
 }

This statement in the `intel_hdcp_gsc_cs_required` function incorrectly assumes that the HDCP GSC is always required when the XE is loaded, without considering the display version. This leads to the requirement being enforced even for display versions lower than 14, where it is not necessary.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
return DISPLAY_VER(xe) >= 14;
```
Reason:
This statement modifies the function to check the display version before determining if the HDCP GSC is required. It ensures that the requirement is only enforced for display versions 14 and above, thus fixing the incorrect assumption and preventing unnecessary enforcement of the HDCP GSC requirement for lower display versions.
